text.p: Australian mineral explorer Metex Resources NL said on Monday it would restructure its Victorian gold interests into a new company, VICGOLD NL, and propose a float of the new company later this year.
The restructuring and float would enable at least A$1.5 million per year to be spent on drilling of existing defined gold targets, Metex said.
Under the proposal, Metex will merge its Victorian interests with contiguous tenements at Sebastian and at Wilsons Hill, which are presently owned by Greater Bendigo Gold Mines Ltd.
VICGOLD will acquire the tenements in exchange for equity consideration, and proceed to raise funds through an underwritten prospectus.
"The capital return... will see the company distribute to its shareholders a significant portion of its VICGOLD shareholding," Metex said.
It said it expected to offer about one VICGOLD 20 cent fully paid ordinary share for every five Metex shares held.
"...I am sure that, with the enhanced expenditure levels, significant new gold discoveries will be made over a short period," Metex managing director Ian Walker said.
Metex shares were 0.5 cents firmer at 29.5 cents at 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT) on Monday.
